private_watchlist.name: Anduril
private_watchlist.note: Talks first reported Jul 24 remain unclosed as of Aug 10 — over 3x the $30.5B mark from just over a year ago and up from the $61B May 2026 Series H (Thrive Capital, a16z). One floated structure would commit investors now to a second, higher-priced raise within about a year if Anduril hits financial benchmarks. Also just picked up the June CCA Increment 1 production award alongside General Atomics.

private_watchlist.name: Shield AI

private_watchlist.name: Saronic

private_watchlist.name: Helsing

bear_case.title: Public-market valuations already stretched
bear_case.description: The US Aerospace & Defense industry trades around 32-33x trailing earnings (CSIMarket) — well above its historical range — while closed private defense-tech deals ran at a median ~18.9x EBITDA / 3.7x revenue through Q1 2026, the richest revenue multiple in four years. Even this week's strong prints (PLTR, KTOS, AVAV) came with sharp round-trips or price-target cuts, a sign public investors are pricing risk into the growth names even as headline multiples climb.

bear_case.title: Capital outrunning production capacity
bear_case.description: Defense tech VC funding topped $14.6B in barely five months of 2026, already a full-year record. Commentators have warned capital is moving faster than governments can convert new technology into recurring production orders — a mismatch that could leave late-stage private rounds overextended.

bear_case.title: Budget politics
bear_case.description: FY27 requests aren't appropriations; NATO's 5%-of-GDP-by-2035 pledge is real money on paper (Germany to €162B/3.2% GDP by 2029, France to 2.25% GDP in 2026) but still depends on political follow-through year after year.

bear_case.title: Downselects hit even the story stocks
bear_case.description: Kratos' exclusion from the June CCA Increment 1 production award (Anduril and General Atomics won instead) is exactly the single-program dependency risk this page has flagged — a beat-and-raise Q2 wasn't enough to stop Cantor cutting its price target. Rheinmetall's Leonardo Iveco-truck deal, tidy-looking months ago, is now snagged by a Leonardo CEO change and rival bidders. AeroVironment separately still faces multiple securities-fraud class actions despite its Locust contract win.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Rheinmetall
positions.note: Record Q2 core profit and an €80B+ backlog were already known, but the new Lockheed ATACMS MoU (Aug 7, first revenue 2028) adds a second growth leg beyond artillery and vehicles. Directly accessible on most UK platforms via European exchange access, unlike the US-listed names here.

positions.name: BAE Systems
positions.note: Upgraded H1 guidance plus a new £5.9B Dreadnought contract; still the most practically accessible name in this sector for you — UK-listed, no PRIIPs friction, no FX wrapper.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: No fresh catalyst this week, but record $42.0B backlog and already-raised FY26 guidance justify holding through the budget cycle on prime-contractor economics rather than a story multiple. Also sits in Space (payloads) — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: Q2 revenue +93% YoY and FY26 guidance raised again — the business keeps beating — but the stock rallied ~30% on the print to ~$156, pushing an already extreme multiple further ahead of the fundamentals; waiting for a better entry. Also anchors the AI sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: AeroVironment
positions.note: The $400M Locust counter-drone award and a new ex-ManTech CFO on the board reinforce the demand and governance thesis, but the stock is already up ~30% in a week on the news and the securities-fraud litigation remains unresolved, so this stays speculative-sized rather than core. Also in Robotics — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Kratos Defense
positions.note: Q2 beat and raised guidance, but Kratos was left out of the June CCA Increment 1 production award (Anduril and General Atomics won instead) — the exact downselect risk this page has flagged — and Cantor cut its price target to $100 from $115 despite the beat. Non-CCA programs (hypersonics, targets) still look solid; waiting for the thesis to reset around what Kratos actually won, not what it didn't.

positions.name: Red Cat Holdings
positions.note: Revenue +520% YoY but net loss widened to $35.3M; growth this fast without a credible path to profitability doesn't answer the dilution question.

positions.name: Ondas Holdings
positions.note: Order momentum continues but the platform is still sub-scale and cash-hungry relative to the story; wait for contracted revenue to catch up to the narrative.
